# GPUI — benchmark report

- branch / commit: `gui/gpui` / `385522a`
- framework + version (crates.io or git rev): `gpui 0.2.2` (crates.io, locked in Cargo.lock)
- renderer actually used: blade (Vulkan) on the NVIDIA RTX 4070 — see nvidia-smi below
  (`./target/release/zuno-gpui` listed as a `C+G` GPU client, 134 MiB VRAM).
  No backend env vars were needed; the app ran natively on Wayland.
- build: `cargo build --release -p zuno-ui-gpui`, first full release build 2m23s,
  binary `target/release/zuno-gpui` 28,487,664 bytes (~27.2 MiB), zero warnings.

## Implementation notes

- list virtualization approach: gpui's `uniform_list` for the Library ▸ Songs
  5,000-track list and for any collection list longer than 60 rows. The row
  render closure is built with `cx.processor(...)` over an `Rc<Vec<TrackId>>`
  snapshot and calls the same `track_row` used by the short plain-row lists, so
  virtualized and non-virtualized rows are pixel-identical. Only the visible
  range is laid out/painted. The bench scroll drives it by poking the list's
  `UniformListScrollHandle` state (`last_item_size` → `base_handle.set_offset`,
  hard jump, no easing) while forcing `View::Library` + `LibraryTab::Songs`.
- what was animated vs static: hover states everywhere (nav, cards, rows,
  buttons); card hover scrim + red play pill via `group_hover`; the playing
  3-bar indicator is driven by the per-frame counter (re-renders every frame
  anyway for the playhead/bench tick). No page-transition animations — view
  switches are instant.
- keyboard interactions shipped: Space play/pause, ←/→ seek ∓10 s, Esc
  (clear search, else back), M mute, Q queue toggle, S shuffle, R repeat-cycle,
  Ctrl-K focus search (+ full cursor/edit keys inside the search field).
  NOT shipped: ↑/↓ row selection, Enter play-selected, PgUp/PgDn scroll,
  `/` search focus.
- visual divergences from the spec (honest): native window decorations instead
  of custom 14 px chrome (spec allows this fallback); New-albums/Library-album
  grids use flex-wrap reflow rather than an exact column count; artist "top
  tracks" is the artist's first album's 10 tracks (core has no play-count
  ranking to sort by); no drag-reorder in the queue (spec: "should"); card art
  uses small rounded corners rather than `rounded-none` squares (gpui `img`
  rounding; 4 px matches the artwork-tile radius token).
- anything the framework made hard/easy that the next evaluator should know:
  - Easy: inline `div().bg().rounded().flex()` styling maps 1:1 onto the design
    tokens; `uniform_list` virtualization is ~10 lines; `svg()` + an
    `AssetSource` gives crisp lucide-style icons with zero assets; Inter loads
    with one `add_fonts` call; the `Application::new().run()` bootstrap just
    works on Wayland+NVIDIA with no env hacks.
  - Hard: gpui 0.2 ships NO text input and NO slider — the search field is a
    ~500-line port of gpui's own `examples/input.rs` (entity +
    `EntityInputHandler` + custom text element) and seek/volume are a custom
    `Slider` element (~100 lines). Three layout gotchas, all found by
    screenshot-bisecting, all with minimal fixes:
    1. a `uniform_list` wrapped in a plain `div().flex_1()` got ZERO height —
       the list must be the direct `flex_1` child (gpui sizes the Auto-behavior
       list by content otherwise);
    2. the Library column needed explicit `flex_1().min_w_0()` — as a flex-row
       child it shrink-wrapped to ~450 px instead of filling the page;
    3. `line_clamp(n)` text with auto width inside a flex ROW measures ZERO —
       clamped text contributes no intrinsic width, so the track title vanished;
       giving the title `flex_1().min_w_0()` (definite width via grow) fixes it.
       Titles inside flex columns (sidebar, cards, player bar) were unaffected.
  - Also: `ElementId` has no `From<String>` (route through
    `ElementId::Name(s.into())`); stop event-bubble with `cx.stop_propagation()`
    (there is no `ClickEvent::stop_propagation`); `TrackView` carries no
    `album_id` (use `library.track(id).album_id` for artwork seeds); bare
    `kill` (SIGTERM) does not reliably terminate the app — use `kill -9`
    (bench exit via `process::exit(0)` is unaffected).

## Honest issues observed

- Two `--bench` runs done while the list was accidentally rendering empty
  (the height bug above) were DISCARDED; only runs C/D above (working list,
  verified on screen) count. Two further runs (A/B) with the same working
  code showed identical RSS (~257 MB) but only ~2% CPU — they ran while the
  session was screen-locked (compositor presenting nothing); C/D ran on the
  live desktop and agree with each other (42–43%), so C/D are the reported
  numbers.
- The machine carries ~15 GB of swap in use by other apps (browser, etc.);
  run-to-run CPU/RSS wobble of a few percent is environmental, not the app.
- gpui does not set a Wayland app-id/title the compositor understands well:
  niri lists the window with unset app-id (title "Zuno" only sometimes); the
  app still tiles, focuses, and fullscreen-renders normally.
- Screenshots: `docs/gui-benchmarks/gpui-home.png` (Home, fullscreen) was taken
  with the final binary; a mid-bench Library ▸ Songs shot confirmed the scroll
  phase shows real mid-list rows. Other views (Search incl. the custom input,
  Artist, Album, Playlist, Settings, Queue overlay) were each launched and left
  5 s with no crash, and the Search/Queue/Home/Songs views were visually
  inspected; the remaining views share the same row/card/shelf widgets.
